questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have prevouisly been on exchange in Granada, which was an amazing experience. So I knew I wanted to go on exchange again in Spain, because I can also speak Spanish. I thought the university in Barcelona had the best opportunities compared to the other agreements in Spain with this master.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the host university sent out very late when the semester would start.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university held some welcome days for international students where we received our proof of arrival which was very effective

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was very hard to find the person who was the correct coordinator for me.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult. I wanted to live in a student housing where it's more safe than in an appartment, but many of them were already booked or very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Search for accommodation as soon as you know when you have been accepted.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is very hard to find and expensive many places.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to select the courses I wanted which they had to approof, but I was responsible for them not clashing in the time schedule. Upon arrival we had welcome days where they gave us a lot of information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is the mobility office where the coordinators can help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Only one course was not offered so I changed to a different one without problem. But one of the courses is for a whole year, which no one told me before arriving.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of when the courses are offered

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was quite high and they expect a lot from you so you need to study

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar but in Barcelona there are more hours of classes and more presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Methodological Seminars and Work- shops, Methods of Qualitative Research in the Study of Immigration, Analysis of Quantitative Research: Statis- tics Techniques in Migratory Studies, The Foundations of Immigration: Politics and Public Policies, Theories of International Mobility and the Incorporation of Immigrants, Immigration law in Europe

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The course Methods of Qualitative Research in the Study of Immigration was very relevant for my master in applied cultural analysis and he professor is very good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Weekend trips where you pay for taxis to and from the airport for instance. From the airport to Poblenou, where I lived it was 35-40 €.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out eating at restaurants is more expensive than you would expect in Spain. And many places they add 10 % in the end on the bill.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The Voluntariat linguistic plan trips and cultural events every weekend which have been really great.
There is also the erasus student network, who also plan events almost everyday but mostly parties but also weekend trips around in Spain.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can really recommend going to the events organized by Voluntariat Linguistic.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can explore many places both in Barcelona in Cataluña or in the rest of Spain. Near to Barcelona you can take the train to Sitges and Girona for instance.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The easiest way to get to know local students is in the classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Only that everything starts very late even on week days.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The sunny weather, the food, the architecture, the beach, the mountains (especially Montserrat, Montjuic and Tipidabo)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be openminded in this way you will get to know more people. Don't be afraid to walk over and talk to someone.
Money of course haha.
Bring both clothes to warm and cold weather. In the winter months it can get quite cold in the evenings.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The attendance in the classes are being noted, and you are only allowed to miss 10 %, in my case 2 classes. If you miss more classes they can fail you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in the beautiful city and getting new friends from all around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit challenging to become friends with the locals. But the international students are very easy to talk to because they are in the same position and situation as yourself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
